Using the parallel execution policy\n`hpx::parallel::execution::par` lets the runtime split the work across all\navailable cores.\n\nThe implementation below\n\n* allocates a temporary vector that holds the reversed input,\n* runs a parallel inclusive scan on that temporary vector,\n* writes the scan result directly into `output` using a reverse iterator,\n* resizes `output` to the correct Example:\n        x = [1, 7, 4, 6, 6, 2]   →   output = [2, 8, 14, 18, 25, 26]\n*/\nvoid reversePrefixSum(std::vector<int> const& x, std::vector<int>& output)\n{\n    const std::size_t n = cases: empty vector.\n\nProvide full code snippet.\n\nAlso mention compile with HPX.\n\nLet\'s craft final answer.assistantfinal**Solution Overview**\n\nThe *reverse prefix sum* (also called a *suffix sum*) of a vector  \n\n```\nx = [x0, x1, … , xN‑1]\n```\n\nis the vector  \n\n```\ny[i] = Σ_{j=i}^{N‑1} xj      (0 ≤ i < N)\n```\n\nThe operation can be expressed as a **scan** (also known as a prefix‑sum) on the\nreversed input:\n\n```\nreverse(x) = [xN‑1, xN‑2, … , x0]\ninclusive_scan(reverse(x)) = [xN‑1,\n                               xN‑1+xN‑2,\n                               …,\n                               Σ_{j=0}^{N‑1} xj]\n```\n\nIf we write the result back through a reverse iterator we obtain the suffix\nsums in the original order.\n\nHPX already provides a parallel `inclusive_scan` algorithm.  \nThe implementation below\n\n* copies the input into the output buffer (so we can work in‑place),\n* runs `hpx::parallel::inclusive_scan` on the **reverse iterators** of that\n  buffer with the `par` execution policy,\n* leaves the result in `output`.\n\nNo auxiliary helper functions are needed – everything is expressed in a\nsingle function body.\n\n---\n\n### Code\n\n```cpp\n#include <hpx/hpx_main.hpp>\n#include <hpx/parallel/algorithm.hpp>\n#include <hpx/parallel/execution.hpp>\n\n#include <vector>\n#include <numeric>   // std::plus\n#include <algorithm> // std::copy\n\n/*  Compute the reverse prefix (suffix) sum of `x` into `output`.\n    The function runs in parallel using HPX.\n    Example:\n        x = [1,7,4,6,6,2]  →  output = [2,8,14,18,25,26]\n*/\nvoid reversePrefixSum(std::vector<int> const& x,\n                      std::vector<int>&       output)\n{\n    const std::size_t n = x.size();\n\n    // Resize the destination and copy the input – we will scan in‑place.\n    output.resize(n);\n    std::copy(x.begin(), x.end(), output.begin());\n\n    // Parallel inclusive scan on the *reversed* view of `output`.\n    // The scan writes its result back through a reverse iterator, so the\n    // final order is the required suffix‑sum order.\n    using hpx::parallel::execution::par;\n    using hpx::parallel::inclusive_scan;\n\n    inclusive_scan(\n        par,                                            // execution policy\n        std::make_reverse_iterator(output.end()),      // first element (x[N‑1])\n        std::make_reverse_iterator(output.begin()),    // one‑past‑last (x[0])\n        std::make_reverse_iterator(output.end()),      // destination (same range)\n        std::plus<int>());                              // binary operation\n}\n\n/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n   Example driver (optional – not required for the library function)\n   ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */\n#ifdef HPX_MAIN\n#include <iostream>\n\nint main()\n{\n    std::vector<int> a{1, 7, 4, 6, 6, 2};\n    std::vector<int> b;\n\n    reversePrefixSum(a, b);\n\n    std::cout << "input : ";\n    for (int v : a) std::cout << v << \' \';\n    std::cout << "\\noutput: ";\n    for (int v : b) std::cout << v << \' \';\n    std::cout << \'\\n\';\n}\n#endif\n```\n\n---\n\n### Why This Is Efficient\n\n| Aspect | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| **Parallelism** | `hpx::parallel::inclusive_scan` with the `par` policy automatically splits the range into chunks, performs local scans, and merges the partial results – the classic work‑efficient parallel scan algorithm (O(N) work, O(log\u202fN) depth). |\n| **In‑place** | No extra temporary vector is allocated besides the output buffer that the caller already provides. |\n| **Cache‑friendly** | The scan works on a contiguous memory region (`output`). Using reverse iterators does **not** change the underlying layout, so the algorithm accesses memory sequentially. |\n| **Load balancing** | HPX’s scheduler distributes the chunks over all available OS‑threads, handling oversubscription and NUMA automatically. |\n| **Correctness** | The algorithm is mathematically equivalent to the definition of a suffix sum; edge cases (empty vector, size‑1 vector) are handled automatically by the library routine. |\n\n---\n\n### Build Instructions\n\nAssuming HPX is installed and `hpx::hpx_main` is linked:\n\n```bash\n# Compile\ng++ -O3 -std=c++20 Small helper struct that holds the four needed values.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    struct Node\n    {\n        int total;   // sum of the whole segment\n        int best;    // best sub‑array sum inside the segment\n        int pref;    // best prefix sum\n        int suff;    // best suffix sum\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2.  Recursive lambda that returns a Node for the range [first, last).\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    const std::size_t grain = 1'000;          // tune for your hardware\n    std::function<Node(std::size_t, std::size_t)> solve =\n        [&](std::size_t first, std::size_t last) -> Node\n    {\n        std::size_t len = last - first;\n\n        // ----- Base case : single element --------------------------------\n        if (len == 1)\n        {\n            int v = x[first];\n            return Node{ v, v, v, v };\n        }\n\n        // ----- Small enough to compute sequentially ----------------------\n        if (len <= grain)\n        {\n            // Linear scan – classic Kadane, but we also keep pref/suff/total.\n            int total = 0;\n            int best  = x[first];\n            int pref  = x[first];\n            int curPref = 0;\n            int suff  = x[last - 1];\n            int curSuff = 0;\n\n            // prefix & total\n            for (std::size_t i = first; maximumSubarray(std::vector<int> const& x)\n{\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 1.  Helper structure that holds the four values needed for merging.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    struct Info\n    {\n        long long sum;   // total sum of the segment\n        long long pref;  // best prefix sum\n        long long suff;  // best suffix sum\n        long long best;  // best sub‑array sum inside the segment\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2.  Sequential Kadane for a small range (grain size).\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    auto sequential = [&](std::size_t first, std::size_t last) -> Info\n    {\n        long long cur_sum = 0;\n        long long cur_best = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long cur_pref = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long cur_suff = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long total    = 0;\n\n        // Kadane while also tracking prefix / suffix.\n        for (std::size_t i = first; i != last; ++i)\n        {\n            long long v = static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n            total += v;\n\n            cur_sum = std::max(v, cur_sum + v);\n            cur_best = std::max(cur_best, cur_sum);\n\n            // prefix: best sum that starts at 'first'\n            cur_pref = (i == first) ? v : std::max(cur_pref, total);\n        }\n\n        // suffix: walk backwards once\n        long long suffix = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long acc    = 0;\n        for (std::size_t i = last; i != first; )\n        {\n            --i;\n            acc += static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n            suffix = std::max(suffix, acc);\n        }\n        cur_suff = suffix;\n\n        return Info{ total, cur_pref, cur_suff, cur_best };\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 3. Helper structure that holds the four values needed for the merge.\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    struct Result\n    {\n        long long sum;   // total sum of the segment\n        long long pref;  // best prefix sum\n        long long suff;  // best suffix sum\n        long long best;  // best sub‑array sum inside the segment\n    };\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2.  Sequential Kadane for a small range – returns a fully populated\n    //     Result object.\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    auto sequential = [&](std::size_t l, std::size_t r) -> Result\n    {\n        long long cur_sum = 0;\n        long long cur_best = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long cur_pref = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long cur_suff = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long total    = 0;\n\n        // Kadane scan while also tracking prefix / suffix information.\n        for (std::size_t i = l; i < r; ++i)\n        {\n            long long v = static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n            total += v;\n\n            // prefix – the best sum that starts at the left border\n            cur_pref = (i == l) ? v : std::max(cur_pref + v, v);\n            // suffix – we will compute it later in a second pass\n            // (simpler: keep the best suffix seen so far)\n            cur_suff = std::max(cur_suff + v, v);\n\n            // Kadane's current best ending at i\n            cur_sum = (i == l) ? v : std::max(cur_sum + v, v);\n            cur_best = std::max(cur_best, cur_sum);\n        }\n\n        // The prefix we computed above is already the maximum prefix.\n        // The suffix we computed is the maximum suffix because we processed\n        // the range left‑to‑right; however we need the suffix that ends at r‑1.\n        // The variable `cur_suff` already holds that value.\n\n        return Result{ total,\n                       cur_pref,\n                       cur_suff,\n                       cur_best };\n    };\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 3. suffix that ends at `r‑1`                             |\n| `best`          | maximum sum of any **contiguous** sub‑array inside the segment        |\n\nThese four numbers are *associative*: given the values for the left half and the right half we can compute the values for the whole interval in **O(1)**:\n\n```\nsum  = left.sum + right.sum\npref = max(left.pref, left.sum + right.pref)\nsuff = max(right.suff, right.sum + left.suff)\nbest = max( left.best,\n            right.best,\n            left.suff + right.pref )\n```\n\nThus the problem reduces to a parallel reduction over the input vector.\n\nThe implementation below\n\n* uses a recursive lambda inside `maximumSubarray` (no external helper functions),\n* spawns the two halves with `hpx::async` when the interval is larger than a\n  configurable cutoff,\n* falls back to a sequential scan for small intervals,\n* works with `long long` internally to avoid overflow and finally returns an `int`.\n\n```cpp\n#include <hpx/hpx_main.hpp>\n#include <hpx/include/async.hpp>\n#include <hpx/include/lcos.hpp>\n\n#include <vector>\n#include <tuple>\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <cstddef>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <limits>\n\n/* Return the largest sum of any contiguous subarray in the vector x.\n   Parallel implementation based on a divide‑and‑conquer reduction.\n   If the vector is empty the function returns 0 (the neutral element).   */\nint maximumSubarray(std::vector<int> const& x)\n{\n    if (x.empty())\n        return 0;\n\n    const std::size_t n      = x.size();\n    const std::size_t cutoff = 1'000; long,long long>(std::size_t,\n                                                                     std::size_t)>\n        solve = [&](std::size_t l, std::size_t r)\n        -> std::tuple<long long,long long,long long,long long>\n    {\n        // --------------------------------------------------------------\n        // Small interval → compute everything sequentially (Kadane style)\n long>::min();\n            long long suff  = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n            long long best  = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n\n            long long curPref = 0;\n            long long curBest = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n\n            for (std::size_t i = l; i < r; ++i)\n            {\n                long long v = static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n                sum += v;\n\n                curPref += v;\n                pref = std::max(pref, curPref);\n                if (curPref < 0) curPref = 0;          // reset for next prefix\n\n                curBest = std::max(curBest + v, v);   // Kadane step\n                best    = std::max(best, curBest);\n            }\n\n            // suffix: walk backwards\n            long long curSuff = 0;\n            for (std::size_t i = r; i-- > l; )\n            {\n                curSuff += static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n                suff = std::max(suff, curSuff);\n            }\n\n            return {sum, pref, suff, best};\n        }\n\n        // --------------------------------------------------------------\n        // Large interval → split and solve halves in parallel\n        // --------------------------------------------------------------\n        std::size_t mid = l + (r - l) / 2;\n\n        // launch left half asynchronously\n        hpx::future<std::tuple<long long,long long,long long,long long>>\n            left_fut = hpx::async(solve, l, mid);\n\n        // solve right half synchronously (helps to keep the recursion depth low)\n        auto right = solve(mid, r);\n        auto left  = left_fut.get();\n\n        // combine the two halves\n        long long left_sum   = std::get<0>(left);\n        long long left_pref  = std::get<1>(left);\n        long long left_suff  = std::get<2>(left);\n        long long left_best  = std::get<3>(left);\n\n        long long right_sum  = std::get<0>(right);\n        long long right_pref = std::get<1>(right);\n        long long right_suff = std::get<2>(right);\n        long long right_best = std::get<3>(right);\n\n        long long sum   = left_sum + right_sum;\n        long long pref  = std::max(left_pref, left_sum + right_pref);\n        long long suff  = std::max(right_suff, right_sum + left_suff);\n        long long best  = std::max({left_best,\n                                    right_best,\n                                    left_suff + right_pref});\n\n        return {sum, pref, suff, best};\n    };\n\n    // Kick‑off the recursion on the whole vector\n    auto result = solve(0, n);\n    long long answer = std::get<3>(result);\n\n    // The problem statement expects an int; clamp to the int range.\n    if (answer > std::numeric_limits<int>::max())\n        return std::numeric_limits<int>::max();\n    if (answer < std::numeric_limits<int>::min())\n        return std::numeric_limits<int>::min();\n    return static_cast<int>(answer);\n}\n```\n\n### Why this is fast\n\n* **Work‑efficiency** – each element participates in exactly `O(log\u202fP)` combine steps\n  (`P` = number of logical cores). Helper data structure – kept inside the function on purpose.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    struct Node\n    {\n        long long total;   // sum of the whole segment\n        long long pref;    // best prefix sum\n        long long suff;    // best suffix sum\n        long long best;    // best sub‑array sum inside the segment\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2.  Merge two adjacent nodes (constant work).\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    auto merge = [](Node const& L, Node const& R) -> Node\n    {\n        Node res;\n        res.total = L.total + R.total;\n        res.pref  = std::max(L.pref, L.total + R.pref);\n        res.suff  = std::max(R.suff, R.total + L.suff);\n        res.best  = std::max({L.best, R.best, L.suff + R.pref});\n        return res;\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 3.  Recursive solver – returns a Node for the range [lo, hi).\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    const std::size_t cutoff = 1024;               // tuneable\n\n    std::function<Node(std::size_t, std::size_t)> solve =\n        [&](std::size_t lo, std::size_t hi) -> Node\n    {\n        std::size_t len = hi - lo;\n\n        // Base case – single element (or empty, which should never happen)\n        if (len == 1)\n        {\n            long long v = static_cast<long long>(x[lo]);\n            return Node{v, v, v, v};\n        }\n\n        // Small enough to compute sequentially → avoid task overhead.\n        if (len <= cutoff)\n        {\n            // Compute the four quantities in a single linear scan.\n            long long total = 0;\n            long long pref   = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n            long long suff   = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n            long long best   = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n\n            long long curPref = 0;\n            long long curSuff = 0;\n            long long curBest = 0;\n\n            // forward pass for prefix & best\n            for (std::size_t i = lo; Sequential Kadane that also fills a Summary – used for the base\n    //     case (small segments).\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    auto sequential = [&](std::size_t lo, std::size_t hi) -> Summary\n    {\n        long long cur_sum   = 0;\n        long long cur_best  = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long cur_pref  = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long cur_suff  = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long total     = 0;\n\n        // Kadane pass – also keep running prefix / suffix information.\n        for (std::size_t i = lo; i < hi; ++i)\n        {\n            long long v = x[i];\n            total += v;\n\n            cur_sum = std::max(v, cur_sum + v);\n            cur_best = std::max(cur_best, cur_sum);\n\n            // prefix: best sum that starts at lo and ends anywhere ≤ i\n            cur_pref = std::max(cur_pref, total);\n\n            // suffix: we compute it later in a reverse pass\n        }\n\n        // reverse pass for suffix (best sum that ends at hi‑1 and starts anywhere)\n        long long rev_sum = 0;\n        for (std::size_t i = hi; i-- > lo; )\n        {\n            rev_sum += x[i];\n            cur_suff = std::max(cur_suff, rev_sum);\n        }\n\n        return Summary{ total, cur_pref, cur_suff, cur_best };\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 3. Helper type that stores the four quantities needed for the merge.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    struct Node\n    {\n        long long sum;   // total sum of the segment\n        long long pref;  // best prefix sum\n        long long suff;  // best suffix sum\n        long long best;  // best sub‑array sum\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2.  Sequential Kadane – used when the segment is small enough.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    const std::size_t SEQ_CUTOFF = 1 << 12;   // ~4096 elements (tune as needed)\n\n    auto sequential = [&](std::size_t lo, std::size_t hi) -> Node\n    {\n        long long cur = 0, best = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long pref = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long suff = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long total = 0;\n\n        for (std::size_t i = lo; i < hi; ++i)\n        {\n            long long v = x[i];\n            total += v;\n\n            cur = std::max(v, cur + v);\n            best = std::max(best, cur);\n\n            pref = std::max(pref, total);               // max prefix up to i\n        }\n\n        // suffix: walk backwards\n        long long suffix_sum = 0;\n        for (std::size_t i = hi; i-- > lo; )\n        {\n            suffix_sum += x[i];\n            suff = std::max(suff, suffix_sum);\n        }\n\n        return Node{ total, pref, suff, best };\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 3.  Recursive parallel worker.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    std::function<hpx::future<Node>(std::size_t, std::size_t)> solve;\n    solve = [&](std::size_t lo, std::size_t hi) -> hpx::future<Node>\n    {\n        std::size_t len = hi - lo;\n        if (len <= SEQ_CUTOFF)\n        {\n            // Small enough → compute directly and wrap in a ready future.\n            return hpx::make_ready_future(sequential(lo, hi));\n        }\n\n        std::size_t mid = lo + len / 2;\n\n        // Launch the two halves in parallel.\n        hpx::future<Node> left  = hpx::async(solve, lo,  mid);\n        hpx::future<Node> right = hpx::async(solve, mid, hi);\n\n        // When both are ready, merge them.\n        return hpx::dataflow(\n            hpx::launch::async,\n            [=](Node const& L, Node const& R) -> Node\n            {\n                Node res;\n                res.sum  = L.sum + R.sum;\n                res.pref = std::max(L.pref, L.sum + R.pref);\n                res.suff = std::max(R.suff, R.sum + L.suff);\n                res.best = std::max({ L.best, R.best, L.suff + R.pref });\n                return res;\n            },\n            std::move(left), std::move(right));\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 4. Sequential Kadane for a small range – used as the base case.\n    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    const std::size_t seq_cutoff = 1 << 12;   // ~4096 elements (tune as needed)\n\n    auto solve_seq = [&](std::size_t lo, std::size_t hi) -> Node\n    {\n        long long cur_sum = 0;\n        long long cur_best = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long cur_pref = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long cur_suff = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long total    = 0;\n\n        // Kadane while also tracking prefix / suffix.\n        long long best_ending_here = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long best_starting_here = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n\n        for (std::size_t i = lo; i < hi; ++i)\n        {\n            long long v = static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n            total += v;\n\n            // prefix: best sum that starts at lo\n            cur_pref = (i == lo) ? v : std::max(cur_pref + v, v);\n            // suffix will be computed later in a second pass\n            // but we can keep a running best_ending_here for the global best\n            best_ending_here = (i == lo) ? v : std::max(best_ending_here + v, v);\n            cur_best = std::max(cur_best, best_ending_here);\n        }\n\n        // Compute suffix in a backward pass\n        long long suffix = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long acc = 0;\n        for (std::size_t i = hi; i-- > lo; )\n        {\n            acc += static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n            suffix = std::max(suffix, acc);\n        }\n\n        // The prefix we computed above is actually the best prefix ending at each\n        // position; the true best prefix for the whole segment is the maximum of\n        // those values. Summary type – holds the four values described above.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    struct Summary\n    {\n        long long total;   // sum of the whole segment\n        long long pref;    // best prefix sum\n        long long suff;    // best suffix sum\n        long long best;    // best sub‑array sum\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2.  Sequential scan for a small segment (grain size).\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    auto sequential = [&](std::size_t lo, std::size_t hi) -> Summary\n    {\n        long long curPref = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long curSuff = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long curBest = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long sum     = 0;\n        long long bestEndingHere = 0;   // Kadane's running sum\n\n        for (std::size_t i = lo; i != hi; ++i)\n        {\n            long long v = static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n            sum += v;\n\n            // prefix: maximum sum from lo up to i\n            curPref = (i == lo) ? v : std::max(curPref, sum);\n\n            // suffix: we will compute it later from the right side,\n            // but we can also keep a running suffix while scanning forward:\n            //   suffix = max(suffix, sum - minPrefixSeen)\n            // For simplicity we recompute it after the loop.\n            // (the extra O(1) work is negligible for the small grain size)\n\n            // Kadane's step for best sub‑array\n            bestEndingHere = std::max(v, bestEndingHere + v);\n            curBest = std::max(curBest, bestEndingHere);\n        }\n\n        // Compute suffix in a second pass (still O(hi‑lo))\n        long long suffix = std::numeric_limits<long long>::min();\n        long long suffixSum = 0;\n        for (std::size_t i = hi; i != lo; )\n        {\n            --i;\n            suffixSum += static_cast<long long>(x[i]);\n            suffix = std::max(suffix, suffixSum);\n        }\n\n        // Prefix is already stored in curPref, but we need the *maximum*\n        // prefix, not the value at the last element.  The loop above already\n        // kept the maximum, so curPref is correct.\n        return Summary{ sum, curPref, suffix, curBest };\n    };\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 3.  Recursive parallel function.\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------------\n    const std::size_t grain = 1024;               // tune for your hardware\n    std::function<Summary(std::size_t, std::size_t)> solve;\n    solve = [&](std::size_t lo, std::size_t hi) -> Summary\n    {\n        std::size_t len = hi - lo;\n        if (len <= grain)               // small enough → sequential\n            return sequential(lo, hi);\n\n        // split in the middle\n        std::size_t mid = lo + len / 2;\n\n        // launch left half asynchronously\n        hpx::future<Summary> left_fut = hpx::async(\n            [&solve, lo, mid]() { return solve(lo, mid); });\n\n        // compute right half in the current thread (helps load‑balancing)\n        Summary right = solve(mid, hi);\n        Summary left  = left_fut.get();   // wait for the left task\n\n        // ----------------------------------------------------------------\n        // 4.
